results.corrected_claim: For a custom bar pinned to an edge over scrolling content, safeAreaBar(edge:alignment:spacing:content:) (iOS/iPadOS/Mac Catalyst/macOS/tvOS/visionOS/watchOS 26.0, not beta, not deprecated) fits better than safeAreaInset. It insets the safe area the same way ("Similar to the safeAreaInset(edge:alignment:spacing:content:) modifier, the content view is anchored to the specified vertical edge of the parent view and its height insets the safe area"). It also "extends the edge effect of any scroll views affected by the inset safe area". safeAreaInset (iOS 15.0) has no scroll-edge-effect behavior. On iPhone Duo (iOS 27.1 beta), read @Environment(\.toolbarVerticalEdge) (HorizontalEdge?) to position custom bars relative to the system's vertical bar.
results.notes: All checked against primary sources. [apple-doc] ScrollEdgeEffectStyle (26.0) JSON: its See Also section 'Configuring scroll edge effects' lists scrollEdgeEffectStyle(_:for:), scrollEdgeEffectHidden(_:for:) and safeAreaBar(edge:alignment:spacing:content:). safeAreaInset does not appear there, and the safeAreaInset page never mentions edge effects. [apple-doc] safeAreaBar has two 26.0 overloads. The base path is the HorizontalEdge one, abstract "Shows the specified content as a custom bar beside the modified view" (the text the finding quotes). The VerticalEdge one (-9hwgb) is the overload that matches the skill's edge: .bottom example, abstract "Shows the specified content as a custom bar above or below the modified view". Its return value is "...adjusting the safe area and scroll edge effects to match." [apple-other] HIG Scroll views (change log June 8, 2026: 'Updated guidance for scroll edge effects'). Full sentence: "If you use custom bars, you might want to add this effect manually if the top layer of your interface needs extra clarity, or adjust its style from automatic to the hard or soft style." Also: "Only use a scroll edge effect when a scroll view is behind floating interface elements." [apple-doc] EnvironmentValues.toolbarVerticalEdge: `var toolbarVerticalEdge: HorizontalEdge? { get }`, iOS/iPadOS 27.1 beta. Abstract: "...Use it to position custom bars or other UI relative to the system's bar placement." Its sample aligns a FloatingToolPalette by this value. [apple-doc] SwiftUI updates, September 2026, 'Controls on the vertical axis' says the same. The HIG's wording is 'might want', so safeAreaInset is not strictly wrong; safeAreaBar is the better-fitting API.

results.corrected_claim: The skill has no iPhone Duo guidance; a grep finds no 'Duo' or vertical-bar content. Everything the finding cites checks out, with one exception: ToolbarVerticalBehavior documents two members, not only .disabled. They are `static let automatic` ("The system determines whether the vertical bar is rendered.") and `static let disabled` ("The vertical bar is disabled."). Both are iOS/iPadOS 27.1 beta, and 27.1 non-beta on Mac Catalyst, macOS, tvOS, visionOS and watchOS. Declarations: `var toolbarVerticalEdge: HorizontalEdge? { get }` and `nonisolated func toolbarVerticalBehavior(_ behavior: ToolbarVerticalBehavior) -> some View`.
results.notes: [apple-other] HIG 'Designing for iPhone Duo' (change log: September 9, 2026, New page). Verbatim matches: "On iPhone Duo, toolbars, tab bars, and navigation controls that are typically at the top and bottom of the display move to the side... The exception is the inner display in portrait, which has enough vertical space to keep standard horizontal bars." Also "In general, don't override the default bar placement.", "Provide both a title and a symbol for each toolbar item that isn't text-only." and "Keep text-based buttons to a minimum. Labels that include text stay in a horizontal bar, so prefer a symbol wherever one works." It points to ToolbarItemVisibilityPriority and ToolbarOverflowMenu, and to ReservedRegion (SwiftUI/UIKit) for the camera and folding regions. [apple-doc] ReservedRegion is iOS 27.1 beta, with kinds occlusion (Dynamic Island, camera) and division (hinge fold). [apple-other] Developer News RSS, 'Prepare and submit your apps for iPhone Duo' (Oct 5, 2026): "iPhone Duo will be available to customers starting October 23, 2026.", "Recompile existing apps with Xcode 27.1, which adds development support for iPhone Duo." and "Starting April 2027, any apps or games submitted will need to include screenshots for iPhone Duo." The Sep 16, 2026 post says: "When iPhone Duo becomes available on October 23, it will run iOS 27.1." [apple-doc] toolbarVerticalBehavior(_:): "Disable the vertical bar only for UIs that are better served by horizontal bars — such as a fullscreen video player with toolbar controls, or a non-scrolling layout like a calculator...". It also says "To hide the bars... use toolbarVisibility(_:for:) instead." [apple-doc] toolbarVerticalEdge: nil "on devices and in contexts where the system never places a vertical bar". [apple-video] Tech talk 111462 is titled 'Raise the bar with iPhone Duo'. Quote: "rather than keeping the count inline, I can use a badge on the inbox to turn an item that displays both text and a symbol into a symbol-only item that feels at home in a vertical bar." Its code uses .badge(7). [apple-doc] SwiftUI updates, Sept 2026, also lists axisBehavior(_:) with ToolbarItemAxisBehavior (.horizontalOnly/.verticalPreferred) and toolbarVerticalCompressionBehavior(_:). A web search was used only as a lead [secondary]; every fact above comes from Apple pages.

results.corrected_claim: Apple's documentation does not support the skill's flat statement that a .search tab puts the search field 'at the top of the screen automatically'. In iOS 26, Apple described the search tab as having "a search field take the place of the tab bar". iOS 27 adds TabRole.prominent: `static var prominent: TabRole { get }`, 27.0 on iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, macOS, tvOS, visionOS and watchOS, not beta. Only one tab can be prominent, and with no explicit .prominent tab a .search tab "may receive the prominent visual treatment by default". The HIG now describes two search-tab styles. The standard tab goes to a landing page with the search field at the top. The button appearance (prominent, a separate trailing button) focuses the field and shows the keyboard with the field above it.
results.notes: [apple-doc] TabRole/prominent JSON: the Discussion text matches the finding verbatim, all platforms 27.0 with beta false. TabRole/search (iOS 18.0) says only "Searchable tab views will prefer to have the first tab with this role implement search...", with nothing about top placement. [apple-doc] SwiftUI updates: June 2026 'Tab bars' says "Set the prominent role on a tab to place the tab in a separate, trailing position of the tab bar." June 2025 'General' says "Set the search role on a tab to take someone to a search tab and have a search field take the place of the tab bar." [apple-other] HIG Search fields (change log June 8, 2026: 'Updated terminology and refined guidance for search as a tab in iOS'). Standard tab: "Tapping the search tab navigates people to a search landing page with a search field at the top." Button appearance: "Tapping the search tab brings focus to the search field and displays the keyboard." Also "the keyboard immediately appears with the search field above it". HIG Tab bars: "A tab bar can include a dedicated search tab at the trailing end." [apple-video] WWDC26 292 'Design intuitive search experiences': "The second option, is to use a button appearance by making Search a prominent tab." WWDC26 278 'Modernize your UIKit app': "The prominent tab is always visible, even when the tab bar collapses during scrolling." UIKit uses UITabBarController.prominentTabIdentifier. WWDC26 269 shows `Tab(role: .prominent) { CartTab() }`. The skill's line 79 in glass-search-field.md says 'takes prominence in the nav layer', which is close to but not identical with the line-85 claim.

results.corrected_claim: On iPhone (iOS 26/27), toolbar search defaults to and is preferred at the bottom, not the nav bar. The skill's own code (.searchable plus .searchToolbarBehavior(.minimize)) configures the bottom-toolbar field: per Apple, "On iPhone, the search field in the bottom toolbar can be configured to appear as a button-like control when inactive." The HIG says to place search at the bottom if there's room, and at the top only when deferring to content at the bottom or when there's no bottom toolbar. Even in a top toolbar (navigation bar), search appears as a toolbar button that animates into a field above the keyboard, or at the top if there isn't space at the bottom.
results.notes: [apple-other] HIG Search fields (June 8, 2026), verbatim: "Place search at the bottom if there's room... Search at the bottom is useful in any situation where search is a priority, since it keeps the search experience easy to reach." Also: "Place search at the top when itʼs important to defer to content at the bottom of the screen, or thereʼs no bottom toolbar." And: "You can include search in a top toolbar, also called a navigation bar, where it appears as a toolbar button. When someone taps it, it animates into a search field that appears either above the keyboard or at the top if there isn't space at the bottom." [apple-video] WWDC26 292 'Design intuitive search experiences', verbatim: "While the bottom toolbar position is preferred, Search can also be placed in a Top Toolbar.", "If you need more than two other toolbar items, search can also start as a button and then animate into a field when tapped." and "Depending on where your Search Field is placed, it will automatically adopt the correct presentation style. Such as using glass when placed in a Toolbar or using standard content styling when placed in the scroll region of your app." [apple-doc] searchToolbarBehavior(_:) (26.0) contains the bottom-toolbar sentence quoted above. SearchToolbarBehavior members are automatic and minimize, so the skill's .minimize is a valid member. SearchFieldPlacement.automatic: "In iOS, iPadOS, and macOS, the search field appears in the toolbar."

results.corrected_claim: iOS 27 adds navigation-bar minimization: `nonisolated func toolbarMinimizationBehavior(_ behavior: ToolbarMinimizationBehavior, for bars: ToolbarPlacement...) -> some View`. It is 27.0 on iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, macOS, tvOS, visionOS and watchOS, not beta. The supported placement is .navigationBar, and an integrated top tab bar minimizes with it. Behaviors are .automatic, .never, .onScrollDown and .onScrollUp. Companion modifiers are toolbarMinimizationSafeAreaAdjustment(_:for:) and toolbarMinimizationRestoration(_:for:), both 27.0. The WWDC26 name toolbarMinimizeBehavior was replaced before release. tabBarMinimizeBehavior(_:) (26.0) is unchanged and not deprecated.
results.notes: [apple-doc] The toolbarMinimizationBehavior(_:for:) Discussion matches the finding verbatim, with example `.toolbarMinimizationBehavior(.onScrollDown, for: .navigationBar)`. [apple-doc] ToolbarMinimizationBehavior (27.0) members: automatic ("...By default, navigation bars on iOS will minimize when the view has a searchable using the toolbarPrincipal placement."), never, onScrollDown and onScrollUp. [apple-doc] toolbarMinimizationSafeAreaAdjustment(_:for:) is 27.0: "Currently, only navigationBar supports customizing the safe area adjustment." [apple-doc] The doc path toolbarminimizebehavior(_:for:) returns 404, so the old name has no shipping page. [apple-other] iOS & iPadOS 27 release notes, SwiftUI > New Features: "You can use toolbarMinimizationBehavior to control bar minimization behavior. This modifier replaces toolbarMinimizeBehavior. (177954148)". UIKit > New Features: "Use UINavigationItem.navigationBarMinimization to control navigation bar minimization behavior. This property replaces UINavigationItem.barMinimizeBehavior and UINavigationItem.barMinimizationSafeAreaAdjustment. (177953926)". [apple-doc] UIKit `var navigationBarMinimization: UIBarMinimization` is 27.0 on iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, tvOS and visionOS. [apple-video] The WWDC26 269 'What's new in SwiftUI' code shows `.toolbarMinimizeBehavior(.onScrollDown, for: .navigationBar)`, the pre-release name. [apple-doc] tabBarMinimizeBehavior(_:) is 26.0 on all platforms, with no deprecation.

results.corrected_claim: The skill's InfoSheet has only `ToolbarItem(placement: .confirmationAction) { Button("Done") { dismiss() } }`, which conflicts with the current HIG (Sheets, updated March 24, 2026). The HIG says not to rely solely on Done, and to pair it with Cancel (or Back in multi-step flows) but never show all three. For single-view sheets, Cancel belongs on the leading edge of the top toolbar and Done on the trailing edge. InfoSheet is read-only, so Done ("dismisses a sheet after completing a task or explicitly saving changes") is the wrong semantic. The better fix is a Close control: the HIG's "Cancel (or Close)" role uses the standard Close symbol, not a 'Close' text label. In SwiftUI that is Button(role: .close) { dismiss() } (ButtonRole.close, iOS 26.0+).
results.notes: [apple-other] HIG Sheets (change log March 24, 2026: 'Updated guidance for button placement'), verbatim: "Provide an alternative to the Done button. If you provide a Done button, always pair it with a Cancel button to give people a clear way to dismiss the sheet without confirming or saving their changes, or a Back button to move to a previous step in the sheet." Also "Relying solely on the Done button implies that completing the task is the only way to exit the sheet, which can feel restrictive or misleading." and "Avoid showing all three buttons — Cancel, Done, and Back — together." And: "In iOS and iPadOS, for sheets with a single view, the Cancel button belongs on the leading edge of the top toolbar. When present, the Done button belongs on the trailing edge." The multi-step tabs say: first step, Cancel leading and Done trailing "in an inactive state"; subsequent steps, "the Back button replaces the Cancel button"; final step, "the Done button becomes active". Anatomy: "The Cancel (or Close) button dismisses a sheet without saving any changes." [apple-other] HIG Toolbars: "Prefer the standard symbols for each, and don't use a text label that says Back or Close." [apple-doc] ButtonRole.close (26.0, all platforms): "Unlike a cancel operation, a close operation doesn't lose progress for a user." Its example puts `Button(role: .close) { dismiss() }` in a sheet's toolbar. [apple-doc] ToolbarItemPlacement.confirmationAction: "In iOS, iPadOS, and tvOS, the system places confirmationAction items in the same location as a primaryAction placement." The HIG names the leading edge for Cancel; it applies to Close only through the 'Cancel (or Close)' wording.
